source_entries.exact_statement: For a connected smooth compact Kähler n-fold (X,omega), alpha=[omega], w in E1(omega), phi in E1_NA(alpha), the actual maximal ray r(w,phi) exists, is ordered in both arguments, and has E(r_t)=E(w)+t E_alpha(phi). The usual datum is the total-potential datum on X^beth retaining supports. A maximal ray having a finite-entropy slice has extended entropy slope H_alpha(phi). Finite H_alpha(phi) admits actual smooth equivariant relatively Kähler cohomological models eta_j strongly converging to phi with H_alpha(eta_j) converging to H_alpha(phi). Calibrated finite-energy mixed slopes, fixed log-canonical tests and joint maximal-ray continuity retain the exact same signature.

concrete_gaps: No construction or nonexistence theorem for the entire unchanged residual P19.2 signature on arbitrary compact Kähler inputs and arbitrary prescribed log-discrepancy-model P data.
The endpoint-preserving construction assumes an explicit one-dimensional infinite chain, initial zero, and a positive-mass endpoint. These additional hypotheses do not close the original atom.
The primary polarized log-discrepancy regularization gives chordal and radial-entropy recovery, without a prescribed endpoint, pole, or mixed-level-mass conclusion.

General relative P-ceiling preservation for unbounded finite-entropy starts is not proved. The entropy theorem does not imply it; a separate infinite-initial-entropy example changes a zero-mass endpoint.

Eventual exactness at each fixed interior level is not exact preservation of the entire continuum at every finite index. General zero-mass P requirements and any fixed-time or genuinely hybrid entropy requirements remain unresolved.
